provider.notes: Registered under the single id 'deepgram' (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1666; gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:397-399); no aliases. default_model records what happens today: the gateway omits an empty model from the request (gateway/src/core/stt/deepgram.rs:486-491) and Deepgram documents base-general, a legacy model, as its default; this is inferred and was not observed on a live call. The plan should make the gateway send an explicit current model and change this field in the same commit. Until then the resolver must use default_model only to find the row for a session that named no model, and the client must keep omitting the model: base-general is not in the streaming specification's closed model list, so sending it explicitly could be rejected. Deepgram has three kinds of model. Nova, Enhanced and Base ids stream on wss /v1/listen, which the gateway already does, and also have a synchronous file endpoint. The six Whisper Cloud ids are file-only and need the call cut into uploaded utterances. The two Flux ids stream only on wss /v2/listen, for which the gateway has no client, and have no file endpoint. The gateway checks no model id today, so Whisper Cloud and Flux ids are accepted at session setup and fail at the vendor. Not given exact rows: the specification value 'custom', and nova-3-pharma, nova-2-phonecall and nova-2-atc, which appear in documentation tables but in neither specification list; they resolve through the family rows or the provider default. Deepgram's rate limits are concurrency limits per project, not per API key, so two keys in one project share them and the gateway cannot see the project from the key. The gateway keeps one circuit breaker per provider name (gateway/src/core/resilience/registry.rs:73-77) and counts a rate-limit response as a failure (gateway/src/core/stt/http_resilience.rs:136-141), so file uploads for Whisper Cloud need a breaker key of their own or they could cut off Nova streaming sessions. The hosts restriction of Whisper Cloud is recorded as constraints.regions on its file transports.

Pipecat separately ships the constant DEEPGRAM_TTFS_P99 = 0.35 s, which is the figure the gateway hard-codes for every Deepgram model (gateway/src/core/stt/deepgram.rs:1424-1426). billing.notes: Only the uploaded seconds are billed, per second with no minimum. Deepgram's pre-recorded prices differ from its streaming prices.

Deepgram quotes prices per minute and bills per second of audio with no minimum; its pricing page says a 14 second file is billed as exactly 14 seconds. This describes the first transport, the streaming socket, on which the gateway forwards every frame including silence; the evidence does not say in so many words that silence on a stream is billed, so bills_silence is left unknown. There is no entry for this model in gateway/src/config/pricing.rs, and lookups there are exact (pricing.rs:466-469), so metering reports no price until one is added. The file transport carries its own billing block.
